# Discrete infection observations

`infection.tsv` records the four actual unchanged Java infection methods on real placed actors.
Source twice and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
The fixture contains 46 cases, 108 snapshots, 324 actor views, and 62 actual calls.
Each snapshot preserves all 154 organism fields, genome identities, ten world observations, and complete statistics.
Statistics coverage includes all 52 instance fields and all 49 public zero-argument getters.

## Comparison contract

Declare the comparison contract and row ledger before the first Rust replay.
Compare scalar, effect, photo, gas, statistics, velocity, and RNG double bits exactly.
Compare integer values, bounds, endpoints, ARGB, reactions, references, and ordering exactly.
Only organism geometry fields `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` use the existing geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Keep explicit NaN classification and signed infinity checks for those five fields.
Do not extend this allowance to other observations.

`H`, G `_reference`, and statistics references identify actual GeneticCode objects.
Equal-valued clones remain distinct identities.
Full G/N rows preserve all genome and gene values.
The separate genetics fixture covers per-Gene mutable-object alias topology.
This fixture does not repeat that independent identity comparison.

Only `_world` and `_visibleWorld` are named `O` collaborator exclusions.
The setup `visible:selected` record is source callback-routing metadata.
World values, statistics, all remaining actor fields, reference topology, and RNG remain comparison obligations.
The separate callback diagnostic supplies zero canonical Rust comparisons.

## Execution and input authority

Compile `tools/reference/InfectionOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.InfectionOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated profile arguments recorded in the provenance.
The helper validates all four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before simulation access.
It rejects existing output directories.
Seven actual negative invocations cover each omitted root, an escaped symlink, and output preservation in both modes.
The existing runner bounds positive processes to 120 seconds and negative processes to 30 seconds.
It cleans each owned process group after execution.

Each case resets actual `Utils.DEF_*` values.
`U` records all 147 mutable primitive settings used by that case.
Initial organism attempts are zero; no genesis or World.time executes.
Mutation settings are minimum `0`, maximum `10000`, and meta rate `0`.
GREEN weight is `7`; the other 45 selectable weights are zero.
The random seed is `827364`.

The helper creates actual headless VisibleWorld and World objects.
It uses real gas-add, paste, and World.addOrganism methods.
Paste/add order is peer at `(1000,1000)`, victim at `(3500,3500)`, and killer at `(2000,2000)`.
Their initial IDs are `0`, `1`, and `2`.
The peer is selected before the first add.
Canonical donors are killer or self; peer remains the separate callback sentinel.
This avoids MainWindow callback branches without replacing collaborators or statistics.
Actual creation/population events, storage insertion, IDs, gases, and statistics remain observed.

Five initial code identities supply the input recipes.
`g0` has GREEN, CYAN, and EYE genes; `g1` and `g2` each have one GREEN gene.
All genes have length `12`, theta `0`, branch `0`, and default reactions.
Symmetry is `1`; mirror, mutation rate, and activity are `0`.
The four numeric modifiers are `1`; all fifteen constructor booleans are false.
Generation is `41` and clade is `root`.
`g3` and `g4` use actual GeneticCode.clone on `g0`.
Full `input` G/N rows retain every supplied field.

The victim holds `g0`; peer holds `g2`.
The killer normally holds `g1`; identity cases paste it with `g0` or `g3` instead.
Each case explicitly supplies victim infection `g3`, saved code `g4`, and infected reproduction threshold `314`.
The first snapshot follows those recorded controls.
Every later `I` input precedes its actual `K` call.
Expected observations come only from real calls, fields, getters, and reference identities.
No copied infection, fruit, counter, or statistics formula supplies an expectation.

## Covered behavior

| Group | Actual observations |
| --- | --- |
| Code overload | Null code, own primary code, equal-valued clone, and repeated identity changes. |
| Donor overload | Distinct donor, self donor, shared primary code, equal-valued distinct code, and copied thresholds. |
| Repetition | Repeated calls deliver distinct events and increment donor counters without deduplication. |
| Saved cache | Every method clears a supplied saved code; replenished cache clears again. |
| Counters | Signed donor-counter wrapping, self-counter wrapping, record ties, later replacement, and infection-sum wrapping. |
| Fruit strength | Strong and weak methods, ordinary and self donors, repeated calls, and positive/nonzero-late branches. |
| Fruit numbers | Odd/negative/extreme thresholds, zero/negative/extreme spore time, truncation, and saturated integer casts. |
| Live records | Shared and distinct code mutation after notification, including metadata and a real gene-length setter. |

The null-code overload still delivers the actual infection event.
It clears saved state and leaves the existing infected reproduction threshold unchanged.
The organism overload increments its donor before the event and copies the donor's current reproduction threshold afterward.
Self infection uses the same actor and primary genome identity.
Repeated infection remains observable even when the infected reference already matches.

Strong and weak fruit methods preserve their separate source arithmetic and cast ordering.
Zero reproduction-late uses the victim's reproduction threshold.
Any nonzero reproduction-late uses the source's segment-based threshold instead.
The positive and negative nonzero cases both observe that alternate branch.
For threshold `101` and spore time `1`, actual strong and weak results are `105` and `4`.
Extreme signed spore times observe saturated minimum/maximum integer results.
The fixture preserves all source integer and long wrapping, without saturation substitutions for counters.

Later metadata and gene edits mutate actual supplied GeneticCode objects.
The actual statistics getters retain their live references to those objects.
Shared primary code edits affect both holders; equal-valued cloned code edits remain separate.
These edits do not request a body rebuild; cached body observations remain actual source state.

The source notifies World before copied or fruit threshold assignment.
Canonical snapshots observe completed calls, without an internal callback probe.
The separate [callback diagnostic](infection_callback.README.md) makes that ordering observable through actual source failure.
It uses no fake World or statistics implementation.

## TSV schema and controls

The fixture reuses the frozen death-family `C/U/I/A/P/K/O/H/W/S/T/G/N/R/E` schema.
Rows are tab-separated ASCII with one newline after each row.
Doubles use sixteen hexadecimal raw IEEE digits; arrays preserve comma-separated order.
Null references use `~`; mutable code identities use `g0` through `g4`.
GeneticCode `O` fields record presence; `H` records their actual identities.

`K` columns are stage, operation, target role, and argument.
The target is `victim` in every recorded case.
Operations are `infectedByCode`, `infectedBy`, `infectedByFruit`, and `infectedByFruitWeak`.
Code arguments are an existing genome label or `~`.
Other arguments are a donor role or `self`.

`I` targets retain `actor:<role>:field`, `statistics:<field>`, and `genome:<label>:field` forms.
GeneticCode controls supply existing labels or `~`.
`genome:<label>:gene0._length` invokes the actual gene setter with the supplied double.
`visible:selected` supplies actual source selection metadata.
`R` peeks at a serialized Random copy without changing the live stream.
It records the following long, integer bounded by `10000`, and double bits.

All 74 original files and 18 prior TSV fixtures retain their recorded hashes.

This fixture accepts no contact color matrix, biological eligibility check, complete world frame, UI behavior, or networking.
It does not accept every infection caller or save-format migration.
Rust comparison and integration results remain separate from this Java observation provenance.
